name: maybe_Video_VlcDispatchEntry2_B
summary: Jump-table dispatch block of the coefficient VLC loop: takes the code index in r12, adds 10 and jumps through the relocated 0x00135418 table after testing the flag byte at 0x02000F00[r6]. Same body as the twin at 0x00135740 (maybe_Video_VlcDispatchEntry2); the block is entered from the coefficient switch tail, so 'Entry2' is a positional label, not a proven role.
evidence: No new named caller or callee: the caller (0x0013BC18) and callee (0x0013BD28) are still maybe_ copies of the same switch tail, and the body is a fragment (code index in in_r12, flag base in unaff_r6), so the dispatch reading cannot be pinned to a specific VLC entry.

name: Video_InterpolateBlock4x4_B
summary: Sub-pixel interpolator of the video decoder: reads four neighbouring packed source words plus the byte one row up, runs a 6-bit fixed-point DDA per byte lane with +0x40>>7 rounding over 16 output samples and writes four packed words. The 0x400 pitch and the taps are the motion-compensation filter kernel.
evidence: The region is now confirmed video by confident neighbours: its direct callee Video_IdctBlock4x4_B and the Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock/Video_DecodeSubblockMask/Video_McPredict*_B names in the same block. The DDA arithmetic is fully readable; the Ghidra body is damaged only in that the sample pointer arrives in r11 (hand-written ABI), which is why the maybe_ was kept. Byte-identical to the twin at 0x001358BC.

name: Video_InterpolateBlock2x2_B
summary: Half-resolution sibling of Video_InterpolateBlock4x4: the same 6-bit fixed-point DDA, but over the 0x200 lanes with two output samples per step, which is what the '2x2' refers to.
evidence: Direct caller Video_DecodeSubblockMask_B and callee Video_IdctBlock4x4_B are confident names, so the kernel sits inside the confirmed decoder; the half-resolution lanes and two samples per step are readable. The Ghidra body is damaged only in the r11 sample-pointer base.

name: Video_BlendPlanesDiag_B
summary: Diagonal neighbour blend of the prediction block: reads the samples at -1, +0xFF, +0x1FF, +0x2FF (and further 0x100 steps in the unrolled tail) and writes 1:2:1 and (a+2b+c+2)>>2 averages as packed words into the lanes 0x100 above.
evidence: No caller (reached by computed jump from the block reconstruction code), but the 1:2:1 / (a+2b+c+2)>>2 arithmetic over the 0x100-byte lanes is fully readable and the twin at 0x0013626C has the same body; the region is confirmed video by Video_IdctBlock4x4/Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock. The Ghidra body is damaged only in the r11 base.

name: Video_BlendPlanesRow_B
summary: Horizontal blend with a one-row-up source kernel: takes the two packed words one lane up (r11-0x100, r11-0xFC) plus the byte at -1 and writes the 1:2:1 averaged packed word at *r11, then repeats down the row.
evidence: No caller, but the taps and the 1:2:1 arithmetic are fully readable and the twin at 0x00136410 has the same body; the region is confirmed video by the confident Video_IdctBlock4x4/Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock names. The Ghidra body is damaged only in the r11 sample-pointer base.

name: Video_BlendPlanesRow2_B
summary: Row-wide unrolled blend kernel: the same 1:2:1 averaging over the 0x100-spaced lanes, unrolled over a whole row of packed words so every intermediate stays in registers.
evidence: No caller, but the taps and the 1:2:1 arithmetic are readable and the twin at 0x00136668 has the same body; the region is confirmed video by the confident Video_IdctBlock4x4/Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock names. The Ghidra body is damaged only in the r11 base.

name: Video_BlendPlanesRow3_B
summary: Second row-wide unrolled blend kernel: averages the 0x100-spaced lanes together with the horizontally adjacent packed words over a whole row.
evidence: No caller, but the taps and the 1:2:1 arithmetic are readable and the twin at 0x001369BC has the same body; the region is confirmed video by the confident Video_IdctBlock4x4/Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock names. The Ghidra body is damaged only in the r11 base.

name: Video_BlendPlanesBlock_B
summary: Block-wide unrolled blend kernel: the same 1:2:1 lane averaging expanded over a whole block so every intermediate stays in registers.
evidence: No caller, but the taps and the 1:2:1 arithmetic are readable and the twin at 0x00136BF4 has the same body; the region is confirmed video by the confident Video_IdctBlock4x4/Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock names. The Ghidra body is damaged only in the r11 base.

name: Video_BlendPlanesFromStream_B
summary: Blend variant used inside the coefficient loop: first advances the decoder state through 0x0013587C and then averages the four lanes into the packed words above.
evidence: Its callee Video_IdctBlock4x4_B is a confident name and the body is the same 1:2:1 arithmetic as the other blend kernels plus one state-advance call; the twin at 0x00136F98 has the same body. The Ghidra body is damaged only in the r11 base.

name: Video_BlendPlanesCorner1_B
summary: Corner (up-left) predictor kernel: averages the up-left byte (-0x101), the left byte (-1) and the two packed words one lane up.
evidence: No caller, but the -0x101/-1/lane-up taps and the 1:2:1 arithmetic are readable and the twin at 0x001372C0 has the same body; the region is confirmed video by the confident Video_IdctBlock4x4/Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock names. The Ghidra body is damaged only in the r11 base.

name: Video_BlendPlanesCorner2_B
summary: Mirrored corner predictor kernel: the same -0x101/-1/lane-up taps with a different tap order.
evidence: No caller, but the taps and the 1:2:1 arithmetic are readable and the twin at 0x001373C4 has the same body; the region is confirmed video by the confident Video_IdctBlock4x4/Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock names. The Ghidra body is damaged only in the r11 base.

name: Video_BlendPlanesCorner3_B
summary: Third corner predictor kernel: the same inputs as Video_BlendPlanesCorner1 with the smallest tap set of the three.
evidence: No caller, but the taps and the 1:2:1 arithmetic are readable and the twin at 0x001374CC has the same body; the region is confirmed video by the confident Video_IdctBlock4x4/Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock names. The Ghidra body is damaged only in the r11 base.

name: Video_FilterPackedBytesRow_B
summary: Per-byte-lane 1:2:1 filter over packed 32-bit words: walks a whole scanline, averaging each byte with its horizontal neighbour and with the byte one row up (r11-0x100) and repacking four samples per word. The four bytes of a word are four consecutive samples, so this is a sample filter, not a per-channel pixel operation.
evidence: Both callers (Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock_B, Video_IdctBlock4x4_B) are confident names, so the filter is inside the confirmed decoder; the 1:2:1 arithmetic is readable and the twin at 0x001375B4 has the same body. The Ghidra body is damaged only in the r11 sample-pointer base.

name: Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4_B
summary: Per-byte-lane 1:2:1 filter over packed 32-bit words: masks four packed words with 0x7F7F7F7F, halves them and recombines with the carry of the next word, a SIMD horizontal 1:2:1 over 16 consecutive samples.
evidence: No caller, but the 0x7F7F7F7F mask-and-average is readable and the twin at 0x00138324 has the same body; the region is confirmed video by the confident Video_IdctBlock4x4/Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock names. The Ghidra body is damaged only in the r11 base.

name: Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4b_B
summary: Per-byte-lane 1:2:1 filter over packed 32-bit words: the same mask-and-average over four words taken in the opposite order.
evidence: No caller, but the 0x7F7F7F7F mask-and-average is readable and the twin at 0x0013849C has the same body; the region is confirmed video by the confident Video_IdctBlock4x4/Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock names. The Ghidra body is damaged only in the r11 base.

name: Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4c_B
summary: Per-byte-lane 1:2:1 filter over packed 32-bit words: the same per-byte average on unaligned byte offsets (-1, +3, +7, +0xB), i.e. over a diagonally shifted sample run.
evidence: No caller, but the unaligned offsets and the 1:2:1 arithmetic are readable and the twin at 0x00138614 has the same body; the region is confirmed video by the confident Video_IdctBlock4x4/Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock names. The Ghidra body is damaged only in the r11 base.

name: Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4d_B
summary: Per-byte-lane 1:2:1 filter over packed 32-bit words: fourth member of the unaligned family, same per-byte average.
evidence: No caller, but the unaligned offsets and the 1:2:1 arithmetic are readable and the twin at 0x001387F0 has the same body; the region is confirmed video by the confident Video_IdctBlock4x4/Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock names. The Ghidra body is damaged only in the r11 base.

name: Video_FilterPackedBytesBlock_B
summary: Per-byte-lane 1:2:1 filter over packed 32-bit words: keeps 15 pointers/accumulators live and applies the mask-and-average to a whole block instead of four words.
evidence: No caller, but the 0x7F7F7F7F mask-and-average over the block is readable and the twin at 0x00138964 has the same body; the region is confirmed video by the confident Video_IdctBlock4x4/Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock names. The Ghidra body is damaged only in the r11 base.

name: Video_FilterPackedBytesBlock2_B
summary: Per-byte-lane 1:2:1 filter over packed 32-bit words: smaller sibling of Video_FilterPackedBytesBlock with fewer live accumulators.
evidence: No caller, but the 0x7F7F7F7F mask-and-average is readable and the twin at 0x00138B30 has the same body; the region is confirmed video by the confident Video_IdctBlock4x4/Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock names. The Ghidra body is damaged only in the r11 base.

name: Video_FilterPackedBytesFrame_B
summary: Per-byte-lane 1:2:1 filter over packed 32-bit words: applies the mask-and-average over a whole frame, walking the four 0x400-spaced lanes (self+1, +0x401, +0x801, +0xC01) with 0x7F7F7F7F as the per-byte lane mask so no lane carries into the next.
evidence: Its callee (maybe_Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock_C) is the same decoder block and the 0x7F7F7F7F mask-and-average over the four lanes is readable; the twin at 0x00138C7C has the same body. The Ghidra body is damaged only in the r11 base.

name: maybe_Os_InitTimeoutBase
summary: One-time init of the global timing record at 0x007AEA48: stores 10x the tick period returned by 0x0010BE98 as a 64-bit value at +0x18, sets the 'have time source' byte at +1 when 0x0010BE20 succeeds, and sets the 'usable' byte at +0 when either is set. Called once from the graphics init path.
evidence: The asm confirms the 64-bit store (add r0,r0,r0,lsl#2 then lsl r0,#1 = x10, strd r0,r1,[r4,#0x18]) and the two readiness bytes, and the only caller is Gfx_InitDefaultTexture; but 0x0010BE98/0x0010BE20 have no readable body, so whether the record is a timeout base or a tick-rate record is still inferred from the x10 scaling.

name: maybe_Gfx_StartPendingView
summary: State-entry helper on the object at self: clears +0x15D0, arms a 3.0f timer in +0x15D4, and when the deadline at +0x15E0 is below f_4C sets f_50=1 and copies f_44 into +0x15D4; a set byte at +0x15DC also applies the default camera/layout entries, and the step ends with f_29=1/f_28=0.
evidence: The only caller is maybe_Field_Talk_SetupFromRecord (scene/talk setup) and the only callee is Camera_ApplyWorkEntriesDefault, so both the 'Gfx_' prefix and the 'pending view' reading are unproven; what the body certainly does is arm a 3.0f timer, test a deadline and apply the default layout.

name: maybe_Actor_StartAnimTimer
summary: Starts the idle animation on the actor at self+0x28, records the clip length from actor+0x320 as the target time in self+0x30, zeroes the accumulated time at self+0x34 and writes the float pi/2 (0x3FC90FDB) into actor+0x158.
evidence: No caller and only one named callee (maybe_Field_Actor_PlayIdleAnimation); the timer reading rests on the duration/elapsed pair at +0x30/+0x34, and what actor+0x158 (pi/2) drives is still unknown.

name: maybe_Actor_EnterMirroredState
summary: Reads the signed value through virtual +0x94, stores its negation through +0x3C, applies arg2 through +0x15C, calls +0x17C, clears the word at +0x118, enables feature 0 through +0xE4 and disables it through +0x120, then calls +0x50(self,0). Returns 1.
evidence: The negation of the +0x94 value is the only mirror evidence and the +0x15C/+0x17C calls are still undecoded; the same +0xE4/+0x120 feature pair is used by the confirmed Actor_NotifyComponentEvent, so the feature toggling is certain but the 'mirrored state' reading is not.

name: maybe_Actor_TogglePartVisibility
summary: Compares the current value from virtual +0x1C with `visible` and, when they differ, enables feature 0x50 through +0xE4 (visible) or disables it through +0x120 (hidden), then clears the word at +0x118.
evidence: The +0xE4/+0x120 enable/disable pair with a feature id is the same one the confirmed Actor_NotifyComponentEvent uses, so the toggle shape is supported; what feature 0x50 is (part, shadow, effect) is still unknown, so the 'PartVisibility' wording stays a guess.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_CreateSpriteNode
summary: Constructor of the UI class whose vtable is 0x0075A3F4: installs the vtable, makes the +4 list head self-referencing, creates the render node at +0x14 (0x00507E00), the sprite mesh at node+0x84 (0x0053DE78) and the sub-node (0x003A7AC8), sets the id word to 0xFF and makes the three list heads at +0x3C/+0x40/+0x44 self-referencing.
evidence: The vtable 0x0075A3F4 is shared with the deleting destructor 0x002BEEE8 (which calls 0x001D8C2C and then the 0x0010F6CC delete thunk), so this is that class's constructor; whether the class is a 'widget' or a 'window' and whether the sprite is its main node is still open.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelState_Enter11OrEIdle
summary: Reuses the 0x11/0x0E panel-state entry (0x001E21D8) and then replaces the duration pair with 0x0072A944+0x40/+0x44, i.e. the same transition with the alternate (idle) duration.
evidence: The region is confirmed as the panel state machine (Ui_PanelState_Enter16/Enter0B/Enter0EOr10/Enter09ForRow/Update are confident names), and the body is a plain call plus two duration stores; which duration the +0x40/+0x44 pair is (idle vs. another wait) is still inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelState_ResetSequence
summary: Resets the panel sequence: releases the card slots at self+0x4C through 0x00379400, clears the running flag f_60 and installs the default duration pair from 0x0072A944+0x30/+0x34.
evidence: The body does three things (slot reset, running-flag clear, default duration), so 'ResetTimers' under-described it; the slot reset through the confident Ui_PokerCards_ResetCardSlots and the shared duration table fix the reading, but the object is a panel sequence, not a timer pair.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelState_SetDurationFromSlot
signature: void maybe_Ui_PanelState_SetDurationFromSlot(UiPanelSequence* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 argument)
summary: Chooses the panel-sequence duration: when the bound slot at f_198 reports 'ready' (0x0062F694 == 1) it re-registers the card slots and uses the short pair 0x0072A944+0x30/+0x34, otherwise it sets the 5-frame wait in f_224 and the long pair +0xB0/+0xB4.
evidence: 0x0062F694 is the same slot-ready query the confident 0x001E25B0 uses and the duration table is shared with the EnterXX helpers, so the branch meaning is supported; the names of the two durations are still unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelState_SetDurationForCard
summary: Releases the overlay handle at f_1B4 and picks the sequence duration pair from 0x0072A944+0x80 when the card id f_240 is 0x2E, or +0x88 otherwise.
evidence: The branch tests one specific card id (0x2E), not a count, and the handle release is the shared overlay release; what makes card 0x2E special (a joker?) is unknown, so the name stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_ResourceHandle_Release
summary: Releases a 3-word handle: when handle[0] is non-null it calls 0x001A6680(handle[0], handle[1], &literal) and then writes -1 into handle[2] to invalidate it.
evidence: The asm shows the release call with a literal third argument and the -1 invalidation; 0x001A6680 is the release helper the named Ui_StartLayoutAnimations/Ui_MessageWindow_TogglePage/Text_UpdateCursorBlink use, so the handle is a UI animation handle rather than a proven Gfx resource.

name: maybe_Work_BuildRecordSelector
signature: void maybe_Work_BuildRecordSelector(u8* out, int value, int flags)
summary: Damaged fragment: writes the larger of two limits at out+8 and fills four type bytes (2/0/2) from the flags argument, forcing the 'any' marker when flags is 0; the decompiled body ends in halt_baddata.
evidence: Still damaged (unaff_r4/r5, halt_baddata) and no caller or named callee, so the field roles come only from the raw asm; the neighbour 0x001F2D10 (maybe_Item_GetStockLevel) places it in the work/save record area but nothing names the selector.

name: maybe_Ui_JumonWindow_CreateEntry
signature: void maybe_Ui_JumonWindow_CreateEntry(int owner, int offset, unsigned char type)
summary: Stamps one spell-window entry object: installs vtable 0x00776D4C (or 0x0076043C for the other variant), writes the type byte to +8/+9/+10, links it at owner+0xDB8 and notifies the entry description.
evidence: The two vtable constants, the +0xDB8 link and the tail call to Ui_JumonWindow_UpdateEntryDescription are readable, but the body is damaged (unaff_r4..r8), so the owner/type/offset split in the signature is still inferred.

name: maybe_Gfx_BitfieldStore
summary: Damaged fragment: tests a value shifted by 0x14 against zero and a mask derived from >>0xB, then stores one byte at (value>>0x14)-0x3A0 before the control flow is truncated (software_interrupt 0xdfe3a0, halt_baddata).
evidence: No caller and no trustworthy callee (the listed callees belong to the enclosing region), and the body is corrupted (in_OV, software_interrupt, halt_baddata), so only the visible bitfield test and single byte store can be named.

name: Ui_BaseObject_Delete
summary: Deleting destructor: runs the shared base cleanup 0x001C33FC (which installs the base vtable and destroys the object at +0xDB8) and then tail-calls the 0x0010F6CC delete thunk, which invokes the virtual deleting destructor.
evidence: The asm is `bl 0x1C33FC; pop {r4,lr}; b 0x10F6CC`, and 0x0010F6CC is the deleting-destructor thunk (sub r1,r0,#8; ldrd r0,r1,[r1]; ldr r2,[r0]; ldr r2,[r2,#4]; bx r2), so the delete reading is certain; the base cleanup is shared with Ui_MessagePage_Dtor and Ui_ListOwner_DtorBase, which fixes the 'base object' part.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_InitTwoAnimRefs
signature: void maybe_Ui_Widget_InitTwoAnimRefs(int self, int descriptor, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Seeds the state triple (1, 7, 2) at +0x4C/+0x50/+0x5E, rebases descriptor+4 through 0x006564C0 into +0x14, and then initialises two 8-byte reference handles at +0x11C/+0x124 through 0x003B3344.
evidence: 0x006564C0 is the text-node setup used by Ui_Layout_RenderTextNode/Ui_MessagePage_LayoutParts and 0x003B3344 is called by Ui_SenrekiWindow_DispatchEvent, so 'two anim refs' is only one of two readings (text-node references fit the same shape); still no caller.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateNamePlateFlag
signature: int maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateNamePlateFlag(UiMessageWindow* self, int update, u32 force)
summary: When the child window at +0x20 is loaded and its +0x184 word is negative, stores (0x00629128(child+0x138) == 0) into the message-window flag byte +0x3F and returns 1; otherwise returns 0.
evidence: 0x00629128 is the helper the named Ui_MessageText_Update uses, which fits a name-plate update, but byte +0x3F is only known to be zeroed in the ctor, so the name-plate meaning is still inferred; the sibling updaters at +0x24/+0x28/+0x30 have the same shape.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_UpdatePagingState
signature: int maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_UpdatePagingState(UiMessageWindow* self, u32 update, u32 force)
summary: Caches the child window's paging value (0x0065114C on child+0x184) into the message-window word +0x48, then, when the helper at +0x2C exists, forwards the page index (0x0065118C) through 0x002F6B0C and remembers the last value in the u16 at +0x4C.
evidence: The getter pair 0x0065114C/0x0065118C still works on child+0x184 and the +0x4C guard is a change-detection cache, but no caller or named callee was added, so 'paging' remains an inference from those two getters.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateWindowStyle
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateWindowStyle(UiMessageWindow* self, u32 update, u32 force)
summary: Caches one style value of the child window at +0x30 into the message-window word +0x50 (0xFFFFFFFF when only `force` is set), reading it through 0x00640248 on the child's attribute block at +0x138.
evidence: Still no caller or named callee; the body is line-for-line the same shape as the +0x20 and +0x28 updaters but works on the third child, so only the slot number is certain and the 'window style' meaning is inferred.

name: Ui_Window_ReleaseEmbeddedChild
summary: Deactivates the sub-object embedded at child+0x1C34 with 0x0061B79C(...,0) and then invokes its virtual +0x18 with 1 (destroy).
evidence: The asm is `add r0,r1,#0x1C34; mov r1,#0; bl 0x61B79C; ldr r0,[r4,#4]; add r0,#0x1C34; ldr r1,[r0]; ldr r2,[r1,#0x18]; mov r1,#1; bx r2`, i.e. deactivate then destroy; Ui_MessageWindow_Ctor destroys the same +0x1C34 sub-object with virtual +0x18(obj,0), which fixes the reading.

name: maybe_Field_MapActorTypeToModelKind
signature: int maybe_Field_MapActorTypeToModelKind(u32 fallback, int type, int subtype)
summary: Pure mapping switch from an actor type id (4..0x1E) plus a subtype to a small kind code (1..0xD for the plain types, 0x2F/0x35..0x3A/0x47/0xA5/0xBE for the type+subtype pairs); unknown combinations return the fallback value.
evidence: All three arguments are unaff_r4/r5/r6, so only the constant pairs survive; the pairs themselves (type 0x12/0x18 with subtype 0/4/6/0x11 -> 0xBE/0x47/0xA5/0x38, 0x2F/0x37) are explicit, but whether the result is a model kind or an animation kind is unknown.

name: maybe_Field_ClearSlotListsAndSwapTag
summary: When *enable is set, walks the ten 0xC-byte slot records at self; then flips the double-buffer tag at +0xD70 to (tag+3)%2 and destroys whatever is still queued in that buffer's list at +0xD58 (virtual +8).
evidence: The +0xD58/+0xD70 double buffer and the virtual +8 destroy slot are the ones the confirmed Field_AttachObjectFromHandle and Field_FlushObjectList use, but the first loop only walks the lists without a visible body, so what 'clear' means stays unclear; the callers (Gfx_ResetViewHandles, Ui_StatusWindow_ReleaseSlots, Cutscene_Teardown) show it is a shared flush.

name: maybe_Ui_Record_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a small UI record: calls the base constructor 0x001E4B98, overwrites the vtable with 0x007598C0, clears the words at +0xC/+0x10 and the bytes at +0x14/+0x15/+0x19, sets the u16 at +0x16 to 0xFFFF and the byte at +0x18 to 0xFF.
evidence: The asm shows `bl 0x1E4B98` (a constructor that installs a vtable and clears +4/+5/+8), then `str r2,[r0]` with the literal 0x007598C0 and the field clears, so this is a derived constructor, not a pool reset: the old name's 'PooledRecord' came from misreading 0x001E4B98 as an allocator.

name: Math_RandomRange
signature: int Math_RandomRange(void* rng, int low, int high)
summary: Rolls a random integer in [low, high] from the 64-bit random state at rng+8: advances the state with the shared step 0x0051B1FC(state+8, 0x7FFFFFFF), takes the remainder modulo (high-low+1) and adds low.
evidence: The asm is `add r0,r0,#8; mvn r1,#0x80000000; bl 0x51B1FC; add r1,r5,#1; bl 0x11CD80; add r0,r1,r4` - the same state+8 / 0x7FFFFFFF roll the confident Math_RandomChanceBelow (0x001CA3A0) and Math_Random_InitState (0x001CA378) use, followed by a modulo and the low offset. The old name's 'wrap' was wrong: nothing wraps, the value is a fresh random draw.

name: maybe_Actor_HasSpecialModelPart
signature: int maybe_Actor_HasSpecialModelPart(ActorModel* self, int slot, int offset)
summary: Predicate over the actor model's part record: true when the part is visible (virtual +0x10), (f_39D & 0x56)==0 and either the part code at +0x74A is 0x54 or the part letter at +0x745 is 'A'/'B'/'C'.
evidence: The named Actor_ApplyModelPartCodes cites this function and its twin 0x001CB744 as the predicates used when applying part codes, but the body is register-starved (coprocessor_function/store, in_cr*), so the slot/offset parameters and the exact part meaning stay uncertain.

name: maybe_Actor_AdjustHeightParam
summary: Adds delta to the s16 at self+0x36, clamped to [0, s16 at self+0x32], skipped when the global UI-busy flag or self byte +0xF1F is set; the delta is zeroed when virtual +0xE8(self,0x73) returns 0.
evidence: No named caller or callee was added; virtual +0xE8 with id 0x73 is the same feature query the flag setters 0x001CBB70/0x001CBDE0 use, so the guard is a per-actor feature check, but what the s16 pair at +0x32/+0x36 measures (height, length, scale) is still unknown.

name: maybe_Actor_SetComponentFlag
summary: Walks the 32 component slots at self+0xE9C: components whose virtual +0xE8 accepts `component` get the +0x134 then +0x120 calls, and a second loop asks every remaining component through +0xF4, falling back to +0x11C.
evidence: The loop is nearly identical to 0x001CB624 (Actor_NotifyComponentEvent), which dispatches an event id over the same 32 slots, so the 'set flag' reading is not proven; the body also has unaff_r4/unaff_r10 spills and the guard call (0x0062BB08) is misnamed.

name: maybe_Actor_QueryChildSlotState
signature: int maybe_Actor_QueryChildSlotState(ActorModel* self, u32 arg2, int slotMask)
summary: 20-byte fragment that scans the 32 child-object slots at self+0xE9C and returns the last non-zero result: for each non-null slot it calls virtual +0xF4 and, when that returns 0, virtual +0x11C.
evidence: Still unreliable: the body reads unaff_r4/r5/r10 and it is the tail loop of 0x001CAFE4 (same +0xF4/+0x11C queries), so the argument split in the signature is a guess.

name: maybe_Actor_SetTwoParameters

name: maybe_Actor_NotifyModelChanged
summary: Asks 0x001CDA78 for the current model/state value and forwards it to the target through virtual +0xEC.
